blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Reliable multi-view forecasting requires videos from different cameras to describe the same evolving 3D scene. To this end, we introduce Video-Point Model (VPM), a world model that conditions on multi-view video histories and a language instruction to jointly forecast future videos from arbitrary viewpoints and the 3D trajectories of persistent scene points. We extend a pretrained world model with camera-conditioned multi-view processing that integrates complementary observations across cameras, and add a trajectory head that predicts how physical points move through time. Each trajectory tracks a single point across all views, and supervising these trajectories alongside video generation therefore anchors appearance changes in every camera to a shared description of 3D motion. To support training and evaluation, we build VPM-Data, a simulation corpus pairing synchronized multi-view videos with persistent point trajectories, and VP-WorldBench, a forecasting benchmark spanning simulated and real environments. We further extend VPM to robot control by adding robot actions as a token modality in the generator. Action tokens share the point-supervised backbone and are denoised jointly with future videos, thereby grounding the policy in the same 3D-aware representation. On VP-WorldBench and existing 4D generation benchmarks, point supervision improves both video fidelity and 3D motion accuracy over a video-only counterpart, and in simulated and real-robot experiments, it also raises the manipulation success of the action-enabled model.
blocks.zh: 可靠的多视图预报需要来自不同相机的视频来描述同一演化中的3D场景. 为此,我们引入了Video-Point Model(VPM),这是一个以多视图视频历史为条件的世界模型,以及从任意观点和持续场景点的3D轨迹联合预测未来视频的语言教学. 我们扩展了预先训练的世界模型,采用相机条件的多视点处理,将相机之间的互补观测整合,并增加一个预测物理点如何穿越时间的轨迹头. 每个轨迹都追踪到所有视线上的单一点, 并监督这些轨迹与视频生成, 为了支持培训和评估,我们建立了VPM-Data,一个模拟设备,将同步多视图视频与持续点轨迹对齐,以及VP-World Bench,一个跨越模拟和真实环境的预测基准。 我们进一步将VPM扩展至机器人控制,在生成器中加入机器人动作作为象征性模式. 行动标志共享点监督主干线,并与未来视频联合解析,从而将政策建立在相同的3D-意识代表中. 在VP-World Bench和现有的4D生成基准上,点表监督在视频专用对等器上既提高了视频忠诚度,也提高了3D运动精度,在模拟和真机器人实验中,它也提高了动作驱动模型的操纵成功率.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
World models aim to anticipate how scenes evolve from past
observations. Recent models pursue this goal by predicting
future videos and, for robot interactions, the associated
actions ( Agarwal et al., 2026 ) .
However, visual plausibility alone does not establish whether
these forecasts describe coherent 3D motion.
Multi-view histories provide richer evidence for predicting
this motion by revealing scene structure and ongoing dynamics
that may be obscured in individual cameras ( Rajič et al., 2025 ) .
To exploit this evidence, a model must relate observations
across cameras to a common prediction of scene evolution.
Its forecasts from arbitrary viewpoints should therefore
depict the same future event, despite differences in
perspective and visibility.

To connect these predictions, we build on geometric
supervision ( Lee et al., 2026b ) for video modeling, including pointmap prediction
and trajectory-derived representation
alignment ( Liu et al., 2026 ; Yang et al., 2026 ) .
Specifically, we investigate jointly forecasting future images
and persistent 3D point trajectories. Because each trajectory
follows the same scene point over time, it provides a common
description of motion across cameras. Learning this motion
alongside image generation encourages the model to relate
appearance changes to the movement of identifiable points.
Unlike conventional tracking, both predictions extend beyond
the observed history, requiring the model to anticipate
correspondences without access to future frames.
Our hypothesis is that learning where scene points will move
helps the visual predictor produce more faithful forecasts.

To support this learning objective, we construct VPM-Data , a simulation corpus covering tabletop
manipulation and urban dynamics. Each sequence pairs synchronized
multi-view videos with persistent point trajectories, camera
geometry, visibility annotations, and language descriptions,
providing aligned supervision for future appearance and motion.
We complement this training corpus with VP-WorldBench ,
an evaluation suite spanning simulated and real environments.
Its simulation component assesses visual and geometric forecasts
on the same held-out events, allowing image quality and motion
accuracy to be examined together.

blocks.en:
We evaluate VPM on our benchmark and existing benchmarks,
assessing future-video quality and 3D trajectory accuracy.
Controlled ablations demonstrate that point supervision improves
visual forecasting. We further investigate whether this benefit
extends to robot control through an action-enabled variant
that jointly learns video prediction, point trajectories,
and robot commands. Across simulated benchmarks and real-robot
experiments, point supervision consistently improves task success
rates of the action-enabled model. Our contributions are threefold: • We introduce VPM, a camera-conditioned model
that jointly forecasts multi-view videos and persistent
3D point trajectories, using explicit point-motion supervision
to improve visual prediction from arbitrary viewpoints. • We develop VPM-Data and VP-WorldBench,
providing aligned visual and geometric training data
and a forecasting evaluation suite spanning simulated
manipulation, urban dynamics, and real-world recordings. • Through extensive experiments and controlled ablations,
we demonstrate the benefits of point supervision for
multi-view forecasting and assess its contribution to
robot action learning in an action-enabled extension.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
Geometry- and Motion-Aware Video Prediction. Auxiliary objectives improve video generation by supervising internal
features with 2D point tracking ( Jeong et al., 2025 ; Lee et al., 2026a ) or
optical flow ( Chefer et al., 2025 ) , or by aligning them with
video and 3D foundation models ( Zhang et al., 2025 ; Wu et al., 2026 ; Han et al., 2026 ) . For multi-view prediction ( Balice et al., 2026 ) ,
SV4D ( Xie et al., 2025 ) synthesizes novel views of observed videos,
Geometry-aware 4D Video Generation ( Liu et al., 2026 ) forecasts RGB and
pointmaps, and X-WAM ( Guo et al., 2026 ) adds actions to multi-view RGB-D
forecasting, while GEM-4D ( Zhou et al., 2026b ) ,
MECo-WAM ( Zhang et al., 2026c ) , and 4D-WAM ( Yang et al., 2026 ) distill
geometry or trajectory fields into video and video–action representations.
Unlike these single-view or per-frame targets, our persistent 3D trajectories
retain point identity across views and time. Closest to ours,
MVTrack4Gen ( Lee et al., 2026b ) supervises novel-view generation with
multi-view point tracking; we differ from this in that we forecast beyond observed frames, lift supervision from 2D to metric 3D, and extend it to action learning.

We build on Cosmos 3 ( Agarwal et al., 2026 ) , whose
Mixture-of-Transformers backbone comprises a reasoner and a
generator. The two towers are initialized from a pretrained
vision-language model and maintain separate layer parameters,
interacting through a joint attention operation.
In the forecasting configuration, the reasoner processes instruction
tokens with causal attention restricted to its own sequence,
while generator tokens attend to both sequences.

blocks.en:
Why 3D point trajectory forecasting helps action prediction. 3D point forecasting supervision consistently improves the action-enabled model
( Table 5 ), which we attribute to three properties.
First, on robot data, trajectories are computed from joint states by forward
kinematics, describing the same motion as actions but grounded in 3D and in
every view, which teaches the backbone to connect visual features with where
the robot will move. Second, they are dense, constraining the robot’s full
future configuration with hundreds of points per timestep rather than one
low-dimensional action. Third, object trajectories, where available, specify
where manipulated objects should go, encoding the task’s intended outcome.
Action tokens, sharing this backbone, thus draw on a representation that
already encodes the robot’s future motion. Supporting this, converting
predicted trajectories into commands via inverse kinematics, without action
tokens, completes unseen real-robot tasks zero-shot ( Figure 4 ).
Though not yet consistent enough for quantitative evaluation, these rollouts
show that forecast trajectories alone carry actionable information
(Appendix A.4 ).

blocks.en: 7 Conclusion and Limitations
blocks.zh: 7. 结论和限制

blocks.en:
We presented VPM, a multi-view world model that jointly forecasts future
videos and persistent 3D point trajectories from posed video histories and
language instructions. With VPM-Data and VP-WorldBench, our experiments show
that supervising where scene points will move improves visual forecasting on
simulated and real benchmarks and carries over to robot action learning.
Limitations remain. Our point supervision covers only the
robot and annotated objects rather than the full scene; skeletal annotations
also omit independent cloth and hair motion. VPM assumes known camera
intrinsics and poses at inference, and its cost grows with the number of
views, as all camera streams share one token sequence. Future work includes
deriving trajectory supervision from real multi-view videos at scale,
extending it to denser, non-rigid content, and relaxing the need for
calibrated cameras.

blocks.en: A.1 Training Details
blocks.zh: A.1 培训细节

blocks.en: We adopt Cosmos3-Nano ( Agarwal et al., 2026 ) as the backbone and follow its Mixture-of-Transformers architecture ( Liang et al., 2024 ) . We train VPM with the three-stage pipeline described in Section 3.5 .
blocks.zh: 我们采用Cosmos3-Nano(Agarwal等人,2026年)作为骨干,并沿用其Mixture-of-Transfors架构(梁等人,2024年). 我们用3.5节描述的三阶段管道训练VPM.

blocks.en:
In Stage 1, we train the generation pathway, camera embeddings, and view frequencies with ℒ FM \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{FM}} on all
multi-view sources, including those without trajectory annotations.
In Stage 2, we freeze the remaining parameters and train only the trajectory head and view frequencies with ℒ track \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{track}} . In Stage 3, we jointly optimize the video backbone and the trajectory head with ℒ forecast \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{forecast}} . The reasoner is frozen throughout all stages. For video supervision, we treat the camera pose of each view as an optional condition. blocks.en:
We evaluate all policies on three pick-and-place tasks with a Franka Research 3 arm and the DROID camera setup (left and right exterior cameras and a wrist camera), as shown in Figure 5 .
All tasks share a tabletop layout with a pile of boxes in the middle, and the object and its goal are placed on opposite sides of the pile so that no single camera shows the whole task ( Figure 6 ).
The robot puts a banana into a basket among other fruits, places a green cup on a plate among cups of other colors, and stacks a small blue cube on top of a red cube next to a green distractor cube, which additionally requires precise placement in height.
Solving these tasks requires fusing the three views into a consistent 3D understanding of the scene, moving across the pile without touching it, and grounding the instruction among same-category distractors.

blocks.en:
To examine whether the forecast trajectories alone carry actionable information, we bypass the action tokens and convert the predicted trajectories directly into robot commands with a training-free two-stage procedure ( Figure 7 and Algorithm 1 ).
We sample N = 128 N{=}128 query points on the robot surface from its kinematic model at the current joint state and project them into both exterior views.
Their trajectories are read from the trajectory head at the third of four denoising steps ( σ ≈ 0.83 \sigma\approx 0.83 ).
We choose this step because σ ≈ 0.83 \sigma\approx 0.83 is the mode of the noise-level distribution used to train the trajectory head, where its predictions are most reliable.
In the first stage, each trajectory is lifted to 3D by triangulating the two views, weighting each observation by its predicted confidence c ^ τ , n v \widehat{c}^{v}_{\tau,n} .
In the second stage, since every query point is attached to a known robot link, we obtain the joint configuration at each future frame by fitting the robot’s forward kinematics (FK) to the lifted points with a robust loss, regularized toward the previous frame for a smooth trajectory.
Each point is weighted by w τ , n w_{\tau,n} , its predicted confidence averaged over views, so that unreliable tracks contribute less to the fit.
The resulting joint trajectory, together with the gripper opening recovered from the finger points, is executed in a receding-horizon manner, without action labels or any robot-specific training.

我们从当前联合状态的动能模型中,对机器人表面的128个NQX128查询点进行取样,并将其投射到两个外景中.
它们的轨迹从四个去诺步骤中的第三个的轨迹头(\\\ 0.83\sigma\ 大约0.83)读取.
我们选择这个步骤是因为 \\\ 0.83\sigma\ 大约 0.83 是用于训练轨迹头的噪音级分布模式, 其预测最可靠。
在第一阶段,通过对两种观点进行三角测量,每个轨道被提升到3D,通过预测的置信度c^,n vv}_{\v}_{\tau,n}k}.

blocks.en: B.2 3D Point Extraction Pipeline from Robot Videos

blocks.en: We describe our pipeline for extracting the 3D point trajectories used to train our model. Our objective is to recover metric, temporally consistent 3D trajectories of action-relevant geometry throughout each manipulation episode. Rather than relying on noisy pseudo-labels from visual point trackers, we construct these trajectories directly from known robot and object geometry together with recorded kinematic states. In particular, robot CAD models provide accurate surface geometry, which can be transformed according to the robot state at each timestep to obtain geometrically grounded 3D point trajectories. We detail this procedure below.

blocks.en: 3D Point Extraction. We begin with the CAD or visual meshes of each robot link and manipulated object. We assume calibrated cameras and a known transformation between the robot base and each camera coordinate frame. For each mesh, we sample surface points using area-weighted triangle sampling. Sampling is performed once in the mesh-local coordinate system with a fixed random seed, and the same points are reused throughout the entire episode. By subsequently transforming these fixed local points according to the corresponding link or object pose at each timestep, we obtain temporally consistent 3D point trajectories without resampling noise.
blocks.zh: 3D点提取器。 我们从每个机器人链接 和被操纵的物体的 CAD 或视网膜开始。 我们假设校准的摄像头 以及机器人基地和每个摄像头坐标框之间的已知变化 对于每个网点,我们通过区域加权三角取样对表面点进行取样。 在网点-局部坐标系统中用固定随机种子进行一次取样,在整个剧集中重复使用相同的点数. 通过随后根据每个时间步对应的链接或物体的姿势来改变这些固定的局部点,我们获得时间上一致的3D点轨迹,而无需再加模噪声.

We allocate a fixed point budget to each action-relevant component: we sample 256 3D points from the whole robot body. In cases where the 3D points of the target object are available, such as in simulation settings, we also sample 256 points from the object being manipulated. blocks.en:
Real-world human benchmark. Our real-world benchmark split comprises 100 newly recorded
10-second sequences featuring three participants in total.
Each sequence includes synchronized multi-view RGB videos,
a sequence of reconstructed 3D surfaces, and camera parameters.
To capture realistic everyday activities, we constructed a 23.1 ​ m 2 23.1\,\mathrm{m}^{2} home-like space furnished with a sink,
cabinets, drawers, a refrigerator, a sofa, tables, and
household objects.
Participants move through the space, lift and carry objects,
open drawers, and set objects down, producing changes in
both human pose and scene configuration.

blocks.en:
Capture system. We capture RGB videos using 48 FLIR industrial cameras
at 30 fps and a resolution of 2048 × 1536 2048\times 1536 pixels.
The camera array combines wide-angle lenses for broad spatial
coverage with standard-field-of-view lenses for capturing detail.
We synchronize image capture across all cameras using an
external hardware trigger.
Before recording, we calibrate camera intrinsics using
Zhang’s method ( Zhang, 2000 ) and estimate extrinsics
using 16 calibration boards distributed throughout the room.
Specifically, perspective- n n -point estimates initialize
the relative camera-board poses, which are linked through
a pose graph in a common metric coordinate system. We further refine the calibration through feature matching
and bundle adjustment using COLMAP ( Schönberger and Frahm, 2016 ) .
The calibrated camera parameters are used for image
undistortion, 3D reconstruction, and as model inputs.

Depth Anything 3 ( Lin et al., 2025 ) .
For all sequences, we optimize the Gaussians for 2,000 iterations
per timestamp before exporting the surfaces.
To reduce holes in the reconstructed surfaces, we extract surface points by back-projecting rendered depth maps rather than directly exporting Gaussian as surface points.

support in each occupied voxel.

blocks.en: D.8 Relation to Existing Resources

blocks.en:
Related resources emphasize complementary annotations and tasks.

blocks.en: E.7 Analysis on Multi-View Video Generation

blocks.en:
To examine how VPM maintains consistency across views, we visualize its cross-view attention in Figure 8 . We select a query grid in one generated view (red box) and overlay its attention map on the other views.
Since Cosmos3-Nano does not natively take multi-view input, we concatenate the views into a single image. For Cosmos3-Nano, the attention scatters over the background and unrelated parts of the robot, and the arm in its generated frame is visibly distorted.
In contrast, the attention of VPM lands on the same hand in each of the other views, matching the
location of the query grid.
This highlights that VPM learns the cross-view correspondence ( An et al., 2025 ; Hong et al., 2024b ; Hong et al., 2024c ; Hong and Kim, 2021 ; Hong et al., 2024a ; Cho et al., 2021 ; Cho et al., 2022 ) and leverages it to generate consistent multi-view videos.
blocks.zh:
透过图8, 我们在一个生成的视图(红框)中选择一个查询网格,并将其注意力图覆盖在其他视图上.
由于Cosmos3-Nano不原生地将多视图输入,所以我们把观点合并为一个图像. 对于Cosmos3-Nano来说,注意力散落在机器人的背景和不相关的部分上,其生成框中的手臂明显扭曲.
反之,VPM的注意力在同一只手上落在了其他各种观点中,与
查询网格的位置。
这突出表明,VPM学习了交叉视图函证(An等人,2025年;Hong等人,2024年b; Hong et al., 2024c ; Hong and Kim, 2021 ; Hong et al., 2024a ; Cho et al., 2021 ; Cho et al., 2022 ) 并利用其生成一致的多景视频.

Results. As shown in Figure 9 , both models improve steadily with more training data, and point supervision improves over the video-only model at every scale.
The gap widens as the data grows on every split. Specifically, the δ avg 3D \delta^{\text{3D}}_{\text{avg}} gap on Real-world Robot grows from 5.76 at 10K to 13.92 at 600K, as the robot datasets add trajectory supervision from real robot episodes.
VPM (V+T) trained on 100K samples already outperforms VPM (V) trained on all 600K samples on every split, e.g. , 70.61 vs. 78.52 FVD on Simulation Robot, indicating that point supervision is a more data-efficient way to improve forecasting than scaling video data alone.

blocks.en:
Setup. Our training data combines three sources ( Table 8 ): VPM-Data (10K samples), robot manipulation datasets with kinematics-grounded point tracks (91K), and open-source videos (504K).
We train VPM (V+T) while leaving out one source at a time and report the change in FVD and δ avg 3D \delta^{\text{3D}}_{\text{avg}} with respect to the model trained on all sources in Figure 10 .
blocks.zh:
设置. 我们的训练数据结合了三个来源(表8):VPM-Data(10K样本),机器人操纵数据集与动能定位点轨(91K),开源视频(504K).
我们训练VPM(V+T),同时一次漏掉一个来源,并报告在图10中所有来源培训的模型中FVD和 ávg 3D\delta\text{3D\text{vg}的变化。

blocks.en: Figure 10: Ablation on training data sources. Relative FVD increase (a) and δ avg 3D \delta^{\text{3D}}_{\text{avg}} decrease (b) of VPM (V+T) when one source is removed from training, measured against the model trained on all sources. Higher is worse.
blocks.zh: 图10:关于培训数据来源的说明。 相对的FVD增加 (a) 和\ avg 3D\ delta\ text{3D\ text{ avg} 减少 (b) VPM(V+T) 当一个来源从培训中删除时, 对照所有来源培训的模型进行测量. 高点更糟糕

blocks.en:
Results. Each source mainly benefits the evaluation domain it covers.
Removing VPM-Data causes the largest degradation on the simulation splits, especially on Simulation General ( + + 48.3% FVD and − - 9.16 δ avg 3D \delta^{\text{3D}}_{\text{avg}} ), since it is the only source that pairs synchronized multi-view urban videos with persistent 3D trajectories. Removing VPM-Data also lowers δ avg 3D \delta^{\text{3D}}_{\text{avg}} on Real-world General by 3.31, suggesting that its accurate simulated trajectories transfer to real human motion.
Removing the robot datasets mainly affects Real-world Robot ( + + 18.2% FVD and − - 12.39 δ avg 3D \delta^{\text{3D}}_{\text{avg}} ), and removing the open-source videos mainly affects Real-world General ( + + 12.2% FVD and − - 6.73 δ avg 3D \delta^{\text{3D}}_{\text{avg}} ).
Removing any source degrades every split, indicating that the three sources are complementary.
blocks.zh:
结果。 每个来源都主要有利于其涵盖的评价领域。
删除 VPM- Data 会导致模拟分裂的最大降解,特别是在模拟一般(++48.3% FVD和−-9.16 avg 3D\delta^{\text{3D}}_{\text{avg}}})上,因为它是唯一将多视图城市视频与持续的3D轨迹对齐的源头. 删除 VPM- Data 也会降低 \ avg 3D\ delta\ text{ 3D\ text{ avg} 在 Real-world General 上以 3.31 表示其精确的模拟轨迹向真人运动的转移.
移除机器人数据集主要影响现实世界机器人(++18.2% FVD和−-12.39 avg 3D\delta\text{3D\text{avg}),删除开源视频主要影响 真实世界通则(++ 12.2% FVD 和 - 6.73 avg 3D\delta^{\text{3D}}_{\text{avg}}}).
删除任何源都会降解每个拆分,表明这三个源是互补的.
